# SOURCES.md — Assignment 6

The A5 version of this file is at tag `a5`
(`fall-2026/jingyao-y/assignment-5/walker-downfall/SOURCES.md`). The A5 cargo
textures (`textures/cargo_panel/rusty_metal_sheet_*_1k.png`, Poly Haven
"Rusty Metal Sheet", CC0, credited there) are no longer drawn by the game. They
are included only because the existing `test_materials` suite loads them; the
fresh-clone check of tag `a6` found that suite failing without them
(TEST-REPORT.md).

## Textures used by the A6 effects

**None sourced, none generated by a model.** Both effect scenes draw with a
32×32 radial `GradientTexture2D` (white centre to transparent edge) defined as
a sub-resource inside `effects/hit_spark.tscn` and
`effects/fire_pit_flames.tscn`; colour ramps are `GradientTexture1D` and scale
curves `CurveTexture`, also inside the scenes. They are textures written as
data in the committed scene files, so no credits file is needed beyond this
record. No image model was used for A6.

## Code and documentation consulted

- Course Example 09 (`examples/09-particle-effects/` on the course repo's
  `main` branch): `tests/particle_cost.gd` was adapted into
  `tests/cost_effects.gd`; its README's account of the 6.9 ms self-measurement
  was the reason for the empty-scene control and the sleep check.
- Godot 4.7.2 itself (ClassDB probe `tests/a6_probe_headless.gd`) for every
  class, property and enum name; the editor's ParticleProcessMaterial →
  ShaderMaterial conversion for `shaders/particles_generated.gdshader`.
- Godot documentation: GPUParticles3D, ParticleProcessMaterial, Movie Maker
  (`--write-movie`).

## Assistance

Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) as the agent: the brief, every prediction and
reading, the reviews, fixtures, documents and commits; six delegated agent
sessions (`prompts/prompt-*.txt`, `sessions/`) built and wired the effects and
wrote the tests and the cost script. The user chose the effects and the upload
scope, gave every runtime verdict and tuning approval, performed the editor
conversion and the Visual Profiler readings. FRICTIONAL.md separates the two in
detail.
